items.basis: The candidate targets removal of particles above 100 microns, but the stated problem is progressive nozzle clogging in 120 flat-fan spray nozzles; typical flat-fan nozzles at 14 bar have throat dimensions on the order of 1-3 mm and fail from accumulation of fines well below 100 microns, meaning the mechanism does not address the dominant clogging vector. The candidate claims the cyclone removes particles above 100 microns and the basin's existing settling volume finishes the separation, but standard mill basins already settle particles above 100 microns effectively due to high settling velocities per Stokes' law; adding a hydrocyclone for a size fraction the baseline already handles yields negligible marginal improvement over doing nothing new. GROUNDED_IN: RECORD "the basin's existing settling volume finishes the separation" | COMPUTATION 100 micron steel scale density ~5000 kg/m3 in water settles at >5 mm/s, exceeding typical basin overflow

The candidate specifies backflushing the underflow collection pot to a scale skip at each roll change, but a roll change requires immediate resumption of 14 bar cooling flow through the return line; interrupting or diverting the return line flow to backflush a pot on the active return loop during a roll change violates the continuous recirculation requirement implicit in the boundary condition that the supply remains untouched while the system operates.
